overview: LaSeR jointly optimizes LLM reasoning and self-verification capabilities by aligning a computationally efficient last-token self-rewarding score with verifier-based rewards using an MSE loss, and integrates self-rewarding signals into the RL advantage estimation to enhance both training and inference-time scaling.

modules.name: Data Processing and Prompting Module
modules.description: Handles the loading and formatting of the mathematical reasoning dataset (e.g., DeepMath-103K), applying model-specific prompt templates for generation, evaluation, and self-verification tasks, and managing the extraction of final answers for the deterministic verifier.

modules.name: Reference Log-Probability Estimator
modules.description: Pre-calculates the constant approximation for the reference model's next-token log-probability of the pre-specified special token. This module samples a subset of data, computes the log-probabilities using the frozen reference model, and averages them to derive the constant used in the simplified self-rewarding score formula.

modules.name: Last-Token Self-Rewarding Score Calculator
modules.description: Implements the core logic to compute the self-rewarding score. It extracts the next-token log-probability of the pre-specified special token at the final token position from the policy model's output, and scales the difference between this value and the pre-calculated constant by the KL coefficient.

modules.name: Self-Rewarding MSE Loss Module
modules.description: Calculates the Mean Squared Error between the last-token self-rewarding scores and the binary verifier-based reasoning rewards. It incorporates class-level loss re-weighting to balance the optimization between correct and incorrect solution samples within each batch.

modules.name: Mixed Advantage Calculator
modules.description: Integrates the verifier-based advantages and the self-rewarding-based advantages using a weighting coefficient. It includes a filtering mechanism that disables the self-rewarding advantage integration if the standard deviation of self-rewarding scores within a group falls below a stability threshold.

modules.name: Training Warm-Up Scheduler
modules.description: Manages the sequential warm-up phases of the training loop. It controls the transition from reasoning-only optimization to self-rewarding optimization, and finally to the joint optimization phase where mixed advantages are activated, based on predefined step milestones.

modules.name: GRPO Base Algorithm Module
modules.description: Implements the Group Relative Policy Optimization baseline, handling the generation of multiple solution samples per query, the computation of group-relative verifier-based advantages, and the standard policy gradient loss with KL divergence constraints.

modules.name: LaSeR Trainer Integration
modules.description: Combines the GRPO base algorithm, the Self-Rewarding MSE Loss, and the Mixed Advantage Calculator into a unified training loop. It orchestrates the forward/backward passes, applies the warm-up scheduler constraints, and manages the joint optimization of reasoning and self-rewarding capabilities.

modules.name: Inference-Time Scaling Module
modules.description: Implements test-time solution aggregation strategies. It supports standard majority voting based on answer frequency, as well as weighted majority voting where the voting weight of each solution is determined by its clipped last-token self-rewarding score.

modules.name: Reasoning Accuracy Evaluator
modules.description: Evaluates the model's reasoning performance by calculating the Pass@1 accuracy. It handles the extraction of final answers from generated solutions, matches them against ground-truth answers using semantic equivalence, and computes the average accuracy across mathematical benchmarks.

modules.name: Self-Verification Evaluator
modules.description: Assesses the model's self-rewarding capability by computing the F1 score. It compares the binary classification derived from the last-token self-rewarding score against the true correctness label from the verifier, calculating the harmonic mean of accuracy on correct and incorrect solutions.

modules.name: Calibration and Correlation Analyzer
modules.description: Analyzes the statistical properties of the self-rewarding scores. It computes the Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC) to measure discriminative power, Expected Calibration Error (ECE) to assess confidence calibration, and Spearman Rank Correlation to evaluate the relationship between scores and response lengths.
